key_insight: Period-shifted dynamic mode decomposition identifies Floquet multipliers and time-periodic modes, with ensemble stacking enabling recovery from partial measurements.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports stability analysis of periodically varying flows and measurements where a single constant snapshot-to-snapshot operator is inadequate.
method: FD applies DMD to fixed-rate snapshots subsampled once per period.
EFD stacks each period’s snapshots into one column to recover shared multipliers and phase-resolved modes.
A period shift collapses Hankel-DMD’s carrier-and-sideband roots onto their Floquet multiplier.
evidence_signal: The methods are verified against known multipliers and illustrated using velocity, scalar, and acoustic-pressure measurements from a swirl-stabilized combustor.
watch_item: Exact recovery requires linear time-periodic dynamics and sufficient observability; nonlinear or noisy data can bias estimated multiplier moduli, which should not be interpreted as decay rates.
paper_title: Floquet Decomposition: Floquet Multipliers and Time-Periodic Modes from Period-Sampled Snapshot Data
